recipes.name: St. Louis Toasted Ravioli
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (25 ounce) package frozen cheese ravioli, thawed
3 cups vegetable oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Heat marinara sauce in a saucepan over medium heat until bubbling; reduce the heat to low and simmer until needed.
Meanwhile, whisk egg and milk together in a small bowl. Whisk bread crumbs and salt together in a second small bowl.
Dip each ravioli in milk mixture, then in bread crumbs to coat.
Heat 2 inches oil in a large, heavy pan until a small amount of breading sizzles and turns brown. Fry ravioli, a few at a time, until golden, about 1 minute per side. Drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle warm ravioli with Parmesan and serve immediately with hot marinara sauce on the side.

raw_recipe.headline: St. Louis Toasted Ravioli
raw_recipe.description: Toasted ravioli traces its roots to St. Louis. This breaded and fried treat is sprinkled with Parmesan cheese and served with marinara sauce for dipping.

video.description: Breaded ravioli are fried and served with marinara sauce.

review.reviewBody: This was a great recipe my family loved it. It takes a little time to fry them so I spread foil on a cookie sheet covered it with a tablespoon of oil breaded the ravioli's and baked them at 350 for about 20 minutes Yummy! Thanks for the recipe.

While this tastes okay, it's absolutely NOT like the traditional St. Louis toasted ravioli, and shouldn't be called by that name! St. Louis toasted ravioli is not cheese filled, it's stuffed full with seasoned beef! The real stuff is much much better!

This was an outstanding dish!!! I followed the advice and kept the ravioli frozen and after I breaded the raviolis I put them in the freezer for 15 minutes, then layered them (one layer at a time)in my deep fryer on 350 for about 1 minute. I served them with gnocchis and a salad for dinner and they were a hit!!!

Just a note.. as a St. Louisan who worked at a popular restaurant there.. it is much easier if you leave the raviolis frozen when you soak and bread them. Then freeze the breading on and fry them frozen.. it is much more user friendly!!

This is a variation of one of the best methods of cooking ravioli and it is unique to St. Louis. You gotta try it. Just try brushing the ravioli in egg white wash and then bread crumbs. And try condensed milk instead of regular milk. But try it. This is a great dish but use a good ravioli or make you own cheese or beef ravioli.

Very yummy recipe and you can indeed use meat ravioli. There aren’t many things more annoyingly idiot than whining about the name of a recipe. Use whatever ravioli you like. What makes it St.Louis style is toasting it with the Italian bread crumbs. Similarly you can call Korbel “champagne” and the earth will continue to turn.

There are great brands of frozen toasted ravioli in your market's frozen food section (the best brand is actually from St. Louis) you can get cheese and beef ravioli...we like the beef. Do yourself a favor and try one...they can be cooked in the oven. Also, using jarred sauce is ok, but to be honest, homemade sauce is not that difficult and tastes so much better. A lot of cooks think a marinara sauce must simmer for hours, but truly, it does not. My recipe takes about a half an hour. It consists of a little olive oil, heated, add fresh garlic, some basil, oregano, thyme, salt and pepper to taste and tomato puree simmer for about 20 minutes...that's it! Ravioli is a great appetizer or works as dinner with a small salad on the side.

I tried this recipe and Giada's recipe on foodnetwork (basic difference being the dip - egg/milk vs buttermilk) and we preferred this just a tad more. I used panko bread crumbs with italian salad seasoning spice mix I had made (1 c bread crumbs to 1 Tbs spice). Also dipped and let the liquid drip off over a cooling rack before breading. Fried in an electric fryer around 330' for ~3 minutes, turning if it seemed to need it. I did the breading prep about 2 hours before I needed to fry them and they came out fine. I'd emphasize getting high quality ravioli for the best result!

I mixed 10 crushed Ritz crackers to the bread crumbs and a tsp parm cheese. Breaded in the morning and put in the freezer for 4 hours. Deep fried for 1 minute. They were awesome! I would make this again and again!

I used evaporated milk to dip these in, as I was out of both whole milk and eggs. It worked fine. I also baked these in a 375 oven for 20 minutes. My 6 year old gobbled these up so fast I thought I was going to have to make another batch for everyone else.
This is NOT St Louis toasted ravioli!! There is no meat in it!! Traditional STL ravioli has a combo of beef, veal and pork which is what distinguishes it from all other raviolis!
I haven’t made it. I will make it, BUT I am from St. Louis and in St. Louis We use MEAT (beef/pork fillings) ravioli not cheese!
I start with beef or meat ravioli. I add Parmesan to the bread crumbs and fry in air fryer- perfect every time!
Not too difficult recipe good for friends gathering as a great snack
I have been using a similar recipe in which you lightly spray the breaded pasta with oil and bake in the oven for 15 minutes. No frying required! Delicious and easy.

Have been born and raised on the Hill (Italian neighborhood) in St. Louis and the home of the toasted ravioli. The main problem with this recipe is that it uses cheese ravioli. Authentic St. Louis Toasted Ravioli uses meat stuffed ravioli.

Someone said that they didn’t see anything “St Louis” about them that they’re all over the place. Well they were a happy mistake created in St Louis, they’ve been around here forever before they became fashionable. Also if you want the true St Louis style used meat stuffed ravioli. Another way to serve them is with melted butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Dip it in the butter then the parm cheese.

Made these with high heat olive oil. I don't see anything "St Louis " about them, I've had these everywhere, even though I just had similar in St Louis's Italian section. Just toasted ravioli really. I suggest you concentrate on the quality of ravioli, and the marinara should be a little sweeter than usual. I'm trying this recipe in my air fryer next.

Doubled the recipe. I used ziploc bags, one for the breadcrumbs the other the eggs and milk. I baked them at 375 for about 25-30 minutes. I've made these dozens of times and the wife always asks for them. They are delicious!

We had this last night for dinner, and it was fantastic! I used a spicy eggplant ravioli and a good marinara that we like. I only had plain Panco, but added Italian seasoning and cayenne. The breading doesn't stick evenly, but maybe that's how it's supposed to be. I deep fried them for just a couple of minutes till brown, turning them halfway. Topped with a bit of fresh parm, served with a nice salad and grilled squashes. Hubs is already asking for it again. Thank you, Barb! This is a fast and easy weeknight meal!
